To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the classroom mastery goal context had positive effects on help seeking, emotional well-being (anxiety), and achievement, whereas the classroom performance-approach goal context had negative effects on achievement and anxiety.

the classroom goal condition had an effect on help seeking, achievement, and test anxiety, and that personal mastery goals were related to achievement, cognitive engagement, help seeking, and emotional well-being, whereas performance-approach personal goals were related only to achievement.

the combined mastery/performance goal condition was most beneficial for help seeking and achievement; that mastery goals were beneficial and performance-approach goal were detrimental for achievement; and that the classroom goal condition was unrelated to the effects of entering personal goal orientation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of classroom goal structures on students' achievement goals, motivation, and achievement.
the motivational effects of multiple goals.
the effects of multiple goals on students' motivation and learning in a classroom context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mastery goals are beneficial for motivation, well-being, engagement, and achievement, performance-approach and performance-avoidance goals are detrimental, and multiple goals can be beneficial.
the current study provides evidence that the combined condition may be beneficial for students' motivation and learning.
the combined condition had the most beneficial pattern of effects, but that this pattern was not due to the presence of performance goals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined mastery/performance approach condition was the best for promoting students' learning and well-being.

the combined mastery/performance approach goal condition is superior to the single mastery or performance approach goal conditions, and that personal mastery goals are beneficial, while personal performance-approaches goals are detrimental.
the combined mastery/performance approach goals were the most beneficial for students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the achievement goal theory debate is too simplistic in that it does not consider the possibility that multiple goals may be used to achieve different outcomes.
it is important for teachers to be cognizant of the goals they are setting for their students, particularly if they want to promote students' motivation, learning, and achievement.
the classroom goal conditions we examined did not produce a detrimental effect on achievement for students with performance-approach orientations.
